Label: Guarded System Trust
Description: This segment generally expresses moderate trust in most national institutions, with response probabilities peaking at a '4' (some trust) for many items like the justice system, auditor, and supreme court. However, they exhibit notably lower trust in political parties and the police, with higher probabilities of expressing 'no trust at all' or 'little trust' for these institutions.

Label: Reserved Institutional Trust
Description: This segment generally expresses moderate trust in most national institutions, frequently selecting a '5' or '6' on the seven-point scale. While outright distrust ('Nada') is rare, strong trust ('Mucho') is also uncommon, suggesting a cautious or reserved level of confidence.

Label: Widespread Distrust
Description: This segment expresses very low trust across nearly all national institutions, with probabilities exceeding 0.60 for 'not at all' on most items. While showing slightly more trust in the president and municipality than other institutions, even these remain relatively low.

Label: Cautious, Low Trust
Description: This segment generally expresses moderate levels of trust in most national institutions, frequently selecting a rating of '3' on the seven-point scale. However, they exhibit notably lower trust in political parties and the police, with a high probability of responding 'not at all' to questions about these institutions.

Label: Presidential & Judicial Trust
Description: This segment expresses strong trust in the president (82% probability of 'A lot') and generally high trust in the justice system, electoral tribunal, armed forces, public ministry, and supreme court (all above 70% probability of 'A lot'). Trust in other institutions is more moderate, with notably lower trust in political parties, the police, and the media.
